study.question: Do memory and grammar configurations yield distinguishable predictions under shared observations?
study.scope: Boundary/length/POS differences covary; not a clean test of structure versus POS priming
study.primary_split: new participants; item families remain shared
study.counterbalance: four cyclic lists cross prime condition and intervening lag; order randomized per participant
study.human_collection: Independent stimulus review and prospective protocol approval are outstanding; local task is a rehearsal
study.instructions: Read the context, then decide whether the displayed continuation can occur after it. Some continuations may be unfinished.
limitations: A grammatical derivation is not a human judgment
All authored items are intended positive; independently reviewed negative controls are needed before a decision experiment

protocol.provenance: synthetic design pilot; not preregistered, not a human experiment

coverage.criterion: Every prime alternative, target and intervening filler must be supported

legacy_ccg_coverage.criterion: Every prime alternative, target and intervening filler must be supported

comparison.split: 3 folds holding out whole participants; lexical families shared
comparison.metric: predictive log density on RT in seconds, including transform Jacobian

comparison.uncertainty: 300 participant bootstrap resamples of fixed held-out predictions; no refitting per draw
comparison.interpretation: Synthetic recovery cannot establish human predictive adequacy

limitations: Memory features predict RT through a fitted observation model; no mechanistic latency claim
Reference grammars are bounded implementation fragments
Model recovery is assessed only on this small design
Boundary, POS and length covary in the two prime conditions
Shared item families limit generalization claims
All items are intended positive; independent negative controls are still needed
DS cues exclude context-only actions; CCG cues include the supplied context in full-span derivations
Non-converged fits are reported but excluded from recovery winners; small score gaps do not establish identification

recovery_summary.interpretation: Descriptive recovery on this design only; no power or human superiority claim
